Q: Upgrading to Compose Multiplatform 1.10.0 no longer resolves compose.runtime A:

This is expected behavior starting with Compose Multiplatform 1.10.0-beta01.

https://kotlinlang.org/docs/multiplatform/whats-new-compose-110.html#unified-preview-annotation

The Compose Multiplatform Gradle plugin has deprecated its dependency aliases (compose.runtime, compose.foundation, compose.ui, etc.).

You now need to declare the libraries explicitly in your version catalog instead of relying on plugin provided shortcuts.

For example, in libs.versions.toml:

compose-runtime = { module = "org.jetbrains.compose.runtime:runtime", version.ref = "composeMultiplatform" }
compose-foundation = { module = "org.jetbrains.compose.foundation:foundation", version.ref = "composeMultiplatform" }
compose-material3 = { module = "org.jetbrains.compose.material3:material3", version.ref = "material3" }
compose-ui = { module = "org.jetbrains.compose.ui:ui", version.ref = "composeMultiplatform" }
compose-components-resources = { module = "org.jetbrains.compose.components:components-resources", version.ref = "composeMultiplatform" }
compose-uiToolingPreview = { module = "org.jetbrains.compose.ui:ui-tooling-preview", version.ref = "composeMultiplatform" }

Then update your module dependencies:

implementation(libs.compose.runtime)
implementation(libs.compose.foundation)
implementation(libs.compose.material3)
implementation(libs.compose.ui)
implementation(libs.compose.components.resources)
implementation(libs.compose.uiToolingPreview)

Once you remove the old compose.* aliases and use direct catalog references, the runtime import will resolve correctly again.

Compose Multiplatform is moving away from hidden alias shortcuts to make dependency management more transparent.

JetBrains has also mentioned that a BOM is planned in the future to simplify version alignment.

If compose.runtime suddenly becomes unresolved after upgrading:

  • It is not a bug

  • The old alias system was deprecated

  • Move dependencies into your version catalog

After migrating, builds work normally again.

Q: Handling audio interruptions that begin, but do not end A:

The usual scenarios where .began fires without a corresponding .ended are: another app taking audio and keeping it, Siri/phone call edge cases, and non-mixable audio categories.

The key takeaway is that you can't rely solely on .ended to recover. Instead, track the interruption state with a flag (isInterrupted), and observe your app returning to the foreground (via applicationDidBecomeActive in UIKit or scenePhase == .activein SwiftUI) as a secondary recovery signal.

Since you're using AVAudioRecorder, on .began: call recorder.pause() (or stop()), set isInterrupted = true, and update your UI to reflect that recording is paused.

On .ended with .shouldResume: reactivate the session and resume recording.

On foreground activation while isInterrupted: attempt setActive(true). If it succeeds, prompt the user to resume rather than auto-resuming. If it fails, the other app still owns audio, so show UI accordingly.

This way you're not stuck waiting for an .ended that may never arrive.

I think this could be super helpful to take a look at for best practices: Handling audio interruptions .

Q: Bazel + C++ project: how to specify working directory for 'run' command A:

bazel run executes the binary within its runfiles tree by default. In Bazel 8.5.0 and later, there is a --run_in_cwd flag for bazel run, which maintains the working directory of bazel for the subprocess.

Possible solutions on older Bazel versions:

  • Don't use bazel run; execute the binary directly.
  • bazel run puts the working directory it was executed from in the $BUILD_WORKING_DIRECTORY environmental variable, so the binary can resolve paths relative to that if desired.
  • On platforms with a POSIX shell, there is a hacky workaround: bazel run --run_under="cd $PWD &&" //some:target

Q: How to get a MySQL field's content with PHP? A:

To find the value of a specific field, just use:

mysqli_fetch_assoc(mysqli_query($conect, $select))['name of the sql field']

mysqli_fetch_field($result) will only show you information about the field, like the type of input, name of the table, name of the column, etc.
